source.author: lucan
source.text: Tum vulnere multo Effugientem animam lassos collegit in artus, Membraque contendit toto, quicumque manebat, Sanguine, et hostilem, defectis robore membris, Insiluit, solo nociturus pondere, puppim.
source.text_original: Tum vulnere multo / Effugientem animam lassos collegit in artus, / Membraque contendit toto, quicumque manebat, / Sanguine, et hostilem, defectis robore membris, / Insiluit, solo nociturus pondere, puppim.
source.text_english: Then, with his many wounds, he gathered up his fleeing life into his weary limbs, and, with whatever blood still remained, strained his limbs through all their length; and, his limbs deprived of strength, he sprang upon the ship, intent on harming it by the mere weight of his body.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: o si mihi sanguis, quantus erat, cum signiferum cratera minantem non leviore Pholum manus haec compescuit auro, primus in aeratis posuissem puppibus arma concussoque ratem gauderem tollere remo.
reuse.text_original: 'o si mihi sanguis, / quantus erat, cum signiferum cratera minantem / non leviore Pholum manus haec compescuit auro, / primus in aeratis posuissem puppibus arma / concussoque ratem gauderem tollere remo.
reuse.text_english: O if only I had had blood, such as it was when this hand checked Pholus, banner-bearer and threatening with the goblet, not with less gold, I would have been the first to place arms on bronze-clad ships and would have rejoiced to lift the vessel with the shaken oar.
